correctness.rationale: The successive forces are order-independent: a currently legal force stays legal until its target is blue. Monotonicity then makes it sufficient to rule out all nine-blue sets and classify the successful ten-blue sets. An independent set-based implementation with sequential forces obtained 3872 minimum sets and seven orbits under the 1920 explicit graph automorphisms. The orbit representatives were matched to the displayed graph types by direct induced-graph isomorphism, and the converse classification was tested over all six-subsets. Building precisely the single-token swaps and running BFS at every orbit representative gives eccentricity 6 throughout and unordered counts 64720, 625440, 2214640, 2986160, 1412976, 190320; orbit weights give the full ordered census, and division by two gives unordered pairs. All defects have Johnson distance 2 and metric distance 3; exactly one partner occurs for each of the 480 P4 plus two isolates configurations and none otherwise. The independent enumeration of all eight-subsets found 80 induced six-cycles with two isolates. The three opposite-pair constructions on each are distinct and together give exact labelled-set equality with the 240 defects, not merely equal totals.
residual_risks: Independent reproduction used exhaustive orbit-weighted BFS, not a rerun of the uploaded all-source C++ program. Exhaustiveness here is for the specified labelled sixteen-vertex graph only.

evidence: Boyer et al. count forcing sets by cardinality; Hogben et al. study the time evolution of forces from a blue set; the AIM paper introduces ordinary forcing for minimum-rank bounds.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Forcing time measures transitions within a single forcing process and the polynomial does not give the relative positions of the minimum sets. Neither implies the new exchange census.

value.rationale: Exchange distances for minimum forcing configurations are a natural reconfiguration invariant with a sharp Johnson lower bound. For this symmetric standard graph the finite metric analysis isolates exactly when the bound fails and ties that failure bijectively to an induced graph structure rather than just producing another size census. The explicit exceptional matching and geometry are a reproducible comparison point for other forcing reconfiguration graphs.
residual_risks: No extrapolation to a family of folded cubes or other Clebsch conventions.
